question: Was Erling Haaland the most valuable player to Manchester City in the early 2024-25 Premier League season (matchweeks 1-15)?

scout_notes.author: The Athletic — Sam Lee
scout_notes.summary: Haaland's output stayed high during City's 7-game winless run (Oct-Nov) — the wobble was structural, not striker-level.

on_off_splits.delta_summary: Rodri ACL injury at the Arsenal match (Sept 22). City's 7-game winless run began three weeks later. PPG dropped from 2.40 with him to 0.90 without — the most catastrophic on/off observed in the league.

dossier.context_notes: Partial-season snapshot (matchweeks 1-15) of the 2024-25 season. Rodri ruptured his ACL on Sept 22 vs Arsenal. City's well-documented collapse (Oct-Nov, 7-game winless run) post-Rodri-injury makes irreplaceability vs output a live test. Haaland output continued normally through the collapse.

__uncertaintyNote__: Likely NO at moderate confidence — Rodri's absence aligns directly with City's collapse, while Haaland's output continued. But partial-season window + structural collapse attribution to one player is contestable. A reasonable judge could call this UNCERTAIN. The framework prizes irreplaceability over output → NO is the on-evidence call but the partial-season nature warrants the uncertainty flag.
